description:
Developing solutions for the Aviation and Aerospace industry since 2010.
 Established in February of 2010, QuAero is a company founded by pilots who are also qualified in engineering, computer science, human factors and other hard sciences, brought together by an EU FP6 project as aviation technical experts. QuAero was created with research and innovation as its company vision and scope. We provide research services and participate in academic studies to help in the advancement of Aviation and Aerospace technologies. Even today, research and innovation are the lifeblood and raison d’etre of QuAero. Following the initial project that brought the company together, QuAero has actively participated in numerous research and innovation projects funded by the Malta Council for Science and Technology, all of which were in collaboration with the University of Malta. We also provide safety management consulting services, training and advisory services on software products. We help our clients create manuals for AOC compliance and train their personnel as required as well as advising on the development of software products for the aviation industry. Through our crew resource management (CRM) services we understand it is essential that pilots learn as much as possible about how best to manage all the resources available to them in the cockpit including other crew-members, procedures, the machine interface and themselves, recognising where they are most vulnerable and where their strengths lie. Lastly, we supply safety software for aviation organisations as well as various other industries, coupled with back-office consultancy such as manuals and operational systems development. QuAero is a licensed reseller of major software brands such as Centrik. Coupled with our expertise, our tech prowess and in-depth knowledge of the software make us a strong ally for our clients, in terms of operational efficiency and compliance.

description: Astrobiome Space SARL is a biotechnology company based in Luxembourg, specializing in space-enhanced formula of microbiome-based products, aiming to improve resilience and high-performance for both humans and plants.
entityDescription:
Astrobiome Space, S.à R.L. is the European HQ of Astrobiome, Inc., registered in Luxembourg in November 2023. 
Astrobiome provides leading-edge solutions for sustainable farming. Their primary products, such as bio-stimulants for plants, leverage space technology to develop super-microbiome-based farming solutions. 
The company's core focus is on harnessing the potential of highly beneficial microorganisms to naturally enhance soil health, stimulate plant growth, and significantly enhance agricultural sustainability, all while reducing the reliance on traditional chemical fertilizers and pesticides. 
The company continuously evolves its products to adapt to rapidly changing climates. This includes innovations such as root treatments and soil microbial therapy, designed not only to improve crop yields and extend shelf life but also to increase the micro-nutrient content of the crops. Astrobiome's approach relies on a feedback loop that integrates Research and Development (R&D) activities with field testing, including extreme environments like space, to expedite experimental processes. 
To achieve these goals, Astrobiome collaborates with a global network of world top scientists, universities, laboratories, Controlled Environment Agriculture (CEA) experts, and progressive farmers. This collaborative approach enhances the company's ability to develop and refine its agricultural solutions in a dynamic and responsive manner. 
The company's structure has been intentionally kept straight forward, serving as an initial framework to facilitate the inclusion of future investors at opportune moments. Currently, the company is under sole ownership, founded by Vera Mulyani, with a dedicated, top world's microbiome scientist team, based in Japan. This team plays a pivotal role in the creation of the unique formula, strain culturing, production, manufacturing, conducting tests, and delivering results for the end product.

A Sustainable City refers to an urban space at the crossroads of the economic, social and environmental pillars necessary for sustainable development. It simultaneously meets citizens’ expectations in terms of comfort, services and resilience, as well as environmental challenges and the needs of future generations.
Within Paris-Vallée de la Marne territory, DDI facilitates serendipitous connections between academia, institutions and businesses with a state-of-the-art research ecosystem in the establishment of a Sustainable City.

At Talogy, we care deeply, we listen. Our experts craft impactfultalent solutionsthat fit your people challenges.
Talogy was born in 1946, with psychology pioneers Floyd E. Ruch, Raymond B. Cattell, Herb Greenberg, and Max Kostick individually launching assessment initiatives to help young adults and war veterans enter the workforce in the years following the second world war. While their industry leading assessment solutions were created in the 1960s, they still play a prominent role in global talent assessment today.
In the 1990s, the world of talent assessment and development started evolving rapidly, and great new solutions were brought to market by the companies founded by these pioneers as well as others. From 2017 onwards, through a series of acquisitions, many of these companies started to come together into one organisation offering an unmatched breadth of talent assessment and development solutions. All leading up to the year 2022, when Talogy as we know it today was born with the purpose to deliver people-focused talent assessment and development solutions to organisations around the world.

entityDescription:
The International Space University develops the future leaders of the world space community by providing interdisciplinary educational programs to students and space professionals in an international, intercultural environment.ISU also serves as a neutral international forum for the exchange of knowledge and ideas on challenging issues related to space and space applications.
It specializes in providing graduate-level training to the future leaders of the emerging global space community at its Central Campus in Strasbourg, France, and at locations around the world. In its one-year Master of Space Studies, two-month Space Studies Program and 5-week Southern Hemisphere-Space Studies Program, ISU offers its students a unique Core Curriculum covering all disciplines related to space programs and enterprises, space science, space engineering, systems engineering, space policy and law, business and management, and space and society. Each of these programs also involve an intense student research Team Project providing international graduate students and young space professionals the opportunity to solve complex problems by working together in an intercultural environment.
Since its founding in 1987, ISU has graduated more than 5000 students from over 110 countries. Together with hundreds of ISU faculty and lecturers from around the world, ISU alumni comprise an extremely effective network of space professionals and leaders that actively facilitates individual career growth, professional activities and international space cooperation.
Building on specialist knowledge already acquired, ISU relates this to all aspects influencing the successful outcome of space development and use. At ISU, programs are:
Interdisciplinary
Broad-based educational programs that encompass all disciplines relevant to space scientific, engineering, economic, regulatory, political and organizational provide students with a multi-dimensional perspective, vital for understanding and effectively dealing with complex space development and utilization issues.
International
Global networking opportunities and intensive teamwork practices at ISU give its diverse student body the edge when performing in competitive and collaborative international space programs.
Intercultural
Interacting with people from a variety of different backgrounds: academic, cultural and national, with varied approaches to problem solving and occasionally conflicting objectives, prepares ISU students for the multicultural environment of today’s world space community.

Each of these programs also involve an intense student research Team Project providing international graduate students and young space professionals the opportunity to solve complex problems by working together in an intercultural environment.
Since its founding in 1987, ISU has graduated more than 5000 students from over 110 countries. Together with hundreds of ISU faculty and lecturers from around the world, ISU alumni comprise an extremely effective network of space professionals and leaders that actively facilitates individual career growth, professional activities and international space cooperation.
Building on specialist knowledge already acquired, ISU relates this to all aspects influencing the successful outcome of space development and use. At ISU, programs are:
Interdisciplinary
Broad-based educational programs that encompass all disciplines relevant to space scientific, engineering, economic, regulatory, political and organizational provide students with a multi-dimensional perspective, vital for understanding and effectively dealing with complex space development and utilization issues.
International
Global networking opportunities and intensive teamwork practices at ISU give its diverse student body the edge when performing in competitive and collaborative international space programs.
Intercultural
Interacting with people from a variety of different backgrounds: academic, cultural and national, with varied approaches to problem solving and occasionally conflicting objectives, prepares ISU students for the multicultural environment of today’s world space community.

entityDescription:
The Fénix Foundation is a Netherlands based non-profit with a mission to leverage technology to support international justice, peace, and accountability. We envision a world where lawyers drive innovation in order to uphold and actualise humanitarian standards. 
The Fénix Foundation’s work is built upon three key pillars. We leverage technology in order to: 
> Empower the lawyers of today by developing cutting-edge legal tools that can disseminate knowledge of international humanitarian, criminal, and human rights law to lawyers on the front-line of accountability work; 
> Educate the lawyers of tomorrow by prioritising cooperation with university legal clinics, where students learn about the intersection between law and the practical application of international humanitarian, criminal, and human rights law; and,
>Secure the rule of law in the digital age by providing high-level trainings for judges and other court officials in order to promote digital literacy, foster a critical understanding of digital tools (including generative AI), and promote knowledge of the value and pitfalls of digital evidence.
